newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco lawyers file petition on Broin damages.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco lawyers file petition on Broin damages.

text.p: Tobacco industry attorneys Monday asked the Florida Supreme Court to force an appeals court to consider whether punitive damages should be part of a $5 billion flight attendants' class action suit against cigarette makers.

The suit, known as Broin vs. Philip Morris et al, was filed on behalf of some 60,000 flight attendants who say they contracted a variety of maladies, including lung cancer, from breathing secondhand cigarette smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.
Last week, the Third Florida District Court of Appeals declined to hear the industry's request that it overturn trial judge Robert Kaye's ruling on punitive damages, saying it lacked jurisdiction.
In a ruling distributed as jury selection began June 2, Kaye denied the industry's motion to deny the flight attendants' request for punitive damages.

The tobacco industry petition filed Monday asked the state's highest court to force the appeals court to take jurisdiction and act on the petition to throw out punitive damages, saying Kaye's action violated their constitutional rights.

The slow process of jury selection in the trial was continuing Monday, with only about 50 potential jurors out of about 200 screened to date having been selected for the pool from which attorneys eventually will take a six-member panel and as many as 12 alternates.
Court officials said they did not expect jury selection would be completed this week.
